recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. A future editorial pass could correct the grammar of "an isModifier elements", but FHIR-15110 is already semantically applied and should not trigger a source-changing reconciliation commit.
issue_request: FHIR-15110 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Security WG change request for STU3 asking for de-identification guidance about interpretation risks when isModifier elements and default-bearing content are redacted. The final resolution narrowed the approved text to adding a warning in the de-identification section that modifying isModifier elements changes resource meaning.
initial_application: The history contains an explicit GF#15110 commit, 7b2b64512052c9a800a59b0ac3cd2cd013659b1b, but that commit added nearby query-parameter access-control guidance rather than the approved isModifier warning. The warning itself appears to have been applied implicitly by df8241d8ed19f08b12c18f34bf71c7bdbf611ef9, which added the de-identification text preserved in source/secpriv-module.html.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml keeps source/secpriv-module.html in the active Security and Privacy module page tree. Later FHIR-52902 work added adjacent guidance that de-identified data may not satisfy normal profile constraints, preserving the FHIR-15110 isModifier warning. For the original default-value concern, current ElementDefinition guidance states that the FHIR specification does not define default values for resources or datatypes, and the final FHIR-15110 resolution did not require adding separate default-value prose.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scope source already satisfies the approved modified resolution, and adding extra links or default-value prose would go beyond the final decision without changing implementer understanding.
